label: Final copy step of length-3 sequences (t=5, L=3)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at the last output step of L=3 sequences (input = 2nd original token, output = 3rd original token). On dev, it is active on ~93% of such steps, and they hold ~90% of activation mass. Strongest when the input token is x (also r), e.g. q x b <DEL> q [x]. Never fires during the original phase or on the delimiter, and never on a first occurrence of a token. Residual weak activations (~10% of mass) occur near the end of copying in longer sequences (to_go 0-2), often on input x, but these are low magnitude and not captured by the predicate. A small fraction (~7%) of L=3 final steps stay inactive.

issues: All the main claims hold up on scoring. Test split for (L==3)&(t==5): P 0.908, R 0.722, F1 0.804, mass recall 0.909. On dev, the unit fires on 2419 of about 2605 L=3 final steps (93%), and those steps hold 0.90 of the mass. Original phase and delimiter: 0 active.
Input x at L=3, t=5 checks out: precision 1.0, and it holds about twice as much mass per step as recall would suggest. Output r at L=3, t=5: precision 0.96.

The 'never fires on the first occurrence of a token' claim is true but says nothing. In the copy phase in_first is never 1, because every copied token has already appeared earlier. Since the unit only fires in the copy phase, the claim follows automatically.

The roughly 9% of missed mass is weak and spread out, not a systematic class. The predicate (L,t) cell with the most misses has precision of only about 1% (L=6 t=11: P 0.011; L=9 t=17: P 0.007; L=4 t=6: P 0.013). Input x outside L=3 with to_go<=2 has P 0.045. Adding input-x clauses gives a best test F1 of 0.786 (with out_tok==r) or 0.44, both below 0.804.

The false positives (L=3 final steps where the unit stays inactive, 240 on test) show no obvious structure. The rate is similar whether or not the token is repeated (in_count==1 P 0.93, in_count>1 P 0.95) and whether or not it is a digit (P about 0.95).

Provenance problem: this verdict is about the store features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store. Its dev split has 99,999 sequences (about 200k total). Nothing here confirms it was built from the 1/5 subsample in features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5, which is what the user asked the baseline to run on. That needs checking separately.
